spec.description: Investigate a specific device

spec.title: 🔍 Select a Device to Investigate
spec.description: Pick a device (or several) from the 'device' dropdown at the top of this dashboard to filter every panel below to just that hostname.

options.content: Use the **device** dropdown at the top to filter these metrics.

spec.title: 📜 Device Specific Alert Log
spec.description: Every alert Loki has logged that mentions this device (matched on hostname substring against the alerts.json stream). This is your full forensic timeline for the device selected above — read top-to-bottom (newest first) to reconstruct exactly what happened and when.

spec.title: AI Anomaly Confidence
spec.description: The IsolationForest ML model's structural outlier score for this device's own bespoke baseline (activates once the device has generated detection_engine.ml_warmup_samples = 5000 events). 0 = looks exactly like this device's normal behavior. Rising toward 1 = increasingly unusual for THIS specific device, even if the traffic would look normal for a different device type.

spec.title: Markov State Transition Anomaly
spec.description: How unlikely this device's current behavioral state is, given its own historical state-transition history (the MarkovStateTracker, see ENGINEERING_MANUAL.md §2.3). A device that has been BENIGN for months has a transition probability to CRITICAL approaching zero — so a sudden jump here is one of the most statistically significant single signals in the whole engine.

spec.title: DNS Query Rate
spec.description: Raw DNS queries per minute from this device. Not inherently good or bad on its own — read it together with DNS Avg Entropy and DNS Z-Score Spikes to the right; a volume spike alongside high entropy is a much stronger DGA signal than volume alone.

spec.title: DNS Avg Entropy
spec.description: Shannon entropy of this device's queried domain names. Per ENGINEERING_MANUAL.md, values above ~4.5 mathematically indicate algorithmically-generated (DGA) domain strings rather than human-typed or CDN-style domains.

spec.title: DNS Z-Score Spikes
spec.description: Standard-deviation (Z-Score) spikes in this device's query rate relative to its own EWMA baseline (baseline_alpha in config.yaml). A Z-Score above 3.0 is a 3-sigma anomaly — statistically, only ~0.3% of normal traffic should ever reach this level.

spec.title: Beaconing Volume Score
spec.description: How closely this device's outbound connection VOLUME matches a periodic beaconing pattern, independent of timing regularity (see Jitter Uniformity Score, next panel). High values here plus low jitter together are the two components of C2 beaconing detection.

spec.title: Jitter Uniformity Score
spec.description: How UNIFORM (low-jitter) this device's connection timing is, measured via Coefficient of Variation. Human/application traffic is naturally irregular; malware C2 check-ins are often suspiciously metronomic. Low jitter + high beaconing volume (left) = classic C2 heartbeat.

spec.title: Cyber Kill-Chain Phase
spec.description: This device's current position in the Cyber Kill Chain: 🟢 Normal → 🟡 Recon → 🟠 Lateral Movement → 🔴 C2 → 🟪 Exfiltration. This is the single fastest way to understand how far an attack has progressed on this specific device.

spec.title: 🎯 Verdict Confidence Over Time
spec.description: This device's live Verdict Confidence (0.0-1.0) -- how certain the engine is in whatever decision-engine verdict it currently holds for this device, set alongside the Verdict itself in decision_engine.py (e.g. a hard-stop match is both severe AND near-certain, ~0.95-1.0; an unconfirmed reputation hit is moderate on both, ~0.40-0.45). The colored bands (shown in blue, not the traffic-light colors Verdict uses) mirror the Verdict Confidence column on the Main Overview ledger: ○ 0-0.39 Low / ◔ 0.4-0.59 Moderate / ◑ 0.6-0.79 High / ● 0.8-1.0 Very High. This is NOT the same as the engine's alert_threshold=6.0, which gates a separate 0-10 aggregate risk score used internally to decide whether to evaluate an alert at all -- containment is driven by the device's Verdict/decision path, not by this confidence value crossing any fixed line.

spec.title: 🌍 Combined External Reputation (TI + AbuseIPDB + VirusTotal)
spec.description: All three independent reputation feeds for this device's contacted IPs plotted together. Because these are independent data sources (verified separately from your own behavioral detections), agreement across two or more of them is very strong corroborating evidence — a device flagged by all three is essentially confirmed-malicious regardless of what your own ML models say.

spec.title: 🛠️ What To Do If This Device Turns Red
spec.description: Step-by-step mitigation guidance tailored to what the panels above are telling you.

options.content:
**This device is showing 🟠 Suspicious or 🔴 Critical activity — what now?**

1. **Check the Kill-Chain Phase panel above.** RECON/LATERAL means it's probing other devices on your LAN — the highest-priority signal to act on, since it can spread. C2/EXFIL means it's likely already compromised and talking to an attacker or leaking data.
2. **DNS sinkholing has already happened automatically** for any confirmed malicious domain (Pi-hole Layer 7 is never gated behind approval). Check the Alert Log below for which domains were involved.
3. **Hardware isolation** (Layer 2 ARP tarpit / Layer 3 router WAN cut) either fired automatically, or — if `interactive_blocking_enabled` is `true` — is waiting for your approval via a Telegram inline button. You can also isolate or release this device directly from the Hostname column's action links on the Overview dashboard's Master Threat Ledger.
4. **After remediating** (running AV, resetting credentials, or simply confirming it was a false positive), release the device. Releasing starts a 1-hour cooldown (`operator_release_cooldown_seconds`) before it can be auto-isolated again — unless it resumes lateral-movement scanning, which bypasses the cooldown immediately.
5. **If this turns out to be a false positive** (e.g. a smart TV doing a firmware check), the CL-AFPE false-positive engine should catch it automatically going forward — see the System Tuning, Healing & Health dashboard to see exactly why it was or wasn't suppressed.

spec.title: 🧠 How This Device Has Been Tuned
spec.description: Section header.

options.content: Everything below is specific to the device(s) selected above ($device). Self-learning/self-healing panels that could NOT be filtered per-device (the underlying Prometheus metric has no hostname label, only a bare device_id or none at all) are noted as fleet-wide in their own description rather than silently showing the wrong thing.

spec.title: Suppress Threshold (Effective)
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_device_threshold_effective for this device -- only set if it has earned its own calibrated profile (>=3 pooled corrections); otherwise the global effective threshold applies instead.

spec.title: ARP-Sweep Threshold (Effective)
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_arp_sweep_threshold_effective for this device.

spec.title: Conn-Abuse Threshold (Effective)
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_conn_abuse_threshold_effective for this device.

spec.title: Long-Conn Threshold (Effective)
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_long_conn_threshold_effective for this device.

spec.title: Device-Profile Corrections by Threshold Key & Source
spec.description: home_ids_autotune_device_profile_correction_total for this device -- filterable by $device now that the metric carries a hostname label (fixed this session; it was already available at the write site in metrics_sync.py, just not threaded through).

spec.title: Sigma-Shift History (Widen vs Tighten)
spec.description: home_ids_fp_sigma_shifts_total for this device, split by direction -- widen (a confirmed false positive made it more lenient) vs tighten (a confirmed threat made it stricter).

spec.title: DNS Query-Rate Baseline vs Live Threshold
spec.description: home_ids_query_rate_baseline_mean (the learned moving average) vs home_ids_query_rate_threshold_limit (the live dynamic alert threshold derived from it) for this device -- never plotted anywhere before.

spec.title: Identity Merges (Lifetime)
spec.description: home_ids_identity_merges_total -- how many times this device's fragmented identity has self-healed (an orphan device_id folded back into this canonical one).

spec.title: Re-ID Migrations (Lifetime)
spec.description: home_ids_identity_reidentify_migrations_total -- MAC-rotation re-identifications this device has been through.

spec.title: Re-ID Ambiguous (Lifetime)
spec.description: home_ids_identity_reidentify_ambiguous_total for this device -- unresolved re-identify candidates needing a reactive capture to resolve.

spec.title: Behavioral Fingerprint Size
spec.description: home_ids_baseline_familiarity_entries_total for this device -- size of its learned port/ASN/domain 'known-normal' fingerprint.

spec.title: Baseline Poisoning & Probation Transitions
spec.description: home_ids_baseline_poisoning_transitions_total and home_ids_probation_transitions_total for this device -- the learning lifecycle over time, not just a point-in-time flag.

spec.title: This Device's ML Model Lifecycle
spec.description: home_ids_ml_warmup_completions_total / _retrain_events_total / _poisoning_rejections_total / _model_invalidations_total -- NOT filterable by hostname (these only carry a bare device_id label); each series here is grouped by device_id instead, so this device's own device_id (visible in the Master Threat Ledger) picks it out of the legend.

spec.title: Transfer-Learning Peer-Seed Count (by Device Type)
spec.description: home_ids_transfer_learning_seeds_total -- this is device_type-level, NOT this exact device: it only fires once, at a NEW device's creation, keyed by device_type rather than device_id. Shown here as the fleet-wide total across all device types for reference; check the boot log for this specific device's own seeding event.

spec.title: Device-Type Reclassifications (Lifetime)
spec.description: home_ids_device_type_reclassifications_total for this device -- how many times its inferred type has changed (e.g. the cold-start 'laptop' fallback replaced once a real hostname resolved).

spec.title: Retro-Hunt Findings (Lifetime)
spec.description: home_ids_retro_hunt_findings_by_device for this device.

spec.title: 📊 More DNS Behavior Signals For This Device

options.content: These are the remaining raw building blocks behind this device's anomaly score -- the ones not already charted above. Read them together, not in isolation: a single spike rarely matters, but several of these moving at once is exactly the pattern the ML model is trained to catch.

spec.title: Blocked & NXDOMAIN Ratios
spec.description: Fraction of this device's DNS queries that were blocked (Pi-hole) or came back NXDOMAIN. A rising NXDOMAIN ratio with no matching rise in blocked ratio can indicate a domain-generation-algorithm (DGA) probing for a live C2 domain that isn't on any blocklist yet.

spec.title: Unique / New / Deep Domain Counts
spec.description: Unique domains queried, domains never seen before this window, and domains with unusually deep subdomain structure (>5 labels). A burst of new + deep domains together is a common DNS-tunneling or DGA fingerprint.

spec.title: Suspicious Domains & NXDOMAIN-TLD Concentration
spec.description: Count of domains flagged as suspicious/DGA-like, and what fraction of this device's NXDOMAIN responses concentrate under a single top-level domain (a sign of one script hammering random subdomains of the same TLD).

spec.title: Other Z-Score Spikes (Blocked / NXDOMAIN / Suspicious / Unique)
spec.description: Same z-score-vs-this-device's-own-baseline treatment as the DNS Z-Score Spikes panel above, for the four signals not already covered there. A z-score above roughly 2-3 means this window is a genuine statistical outlier for this specific device, not just generically high.

spec.title: Threat Intel Match (This Device)
spec.description: Did this device's most recent traffic hit a known-bad IOC on any loaded threat-intel feed? This is the raw yes/no behind the Combined External Reputation score above -- 1 means a real match happened, 0 means clean (or TI not yet ready -- check the fleet-wide TI Engine Ready stat on System Health).
